the_trade_off_made: We favored impact and deadline urgency over revenue, placing the free‑plan data loss ahead of high‑paying enterprise tickets. This sacrifices short‑term satisfaction of big spenders and may delay their roadmap items.
hardest_call: Putting the security incident (TICK-00771) third instead of second was the closest call; it could reasonably have been ranked above the massive data loss because breaches have long‑term security ramifications.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.why: Damage captures user impact, work blockage and severity, which best distinguishes the truly critical tickets in this mixed set.

rejected.money: Leading with money would have pushed the free‑plan data loss and security incident down, missing their real harm; it would have correctly prioritized enterprise revenue.
rejected.deadline: A pure deadline focus would have elevated the overdue export but could have left the security breach lower than required by policy.
rejected.fairness: Fairness rankings would have shuffled tickets based on past interactions, ignoring the magnitude of current harm.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.what_it_costs_us: Prioritizing damage may delay work for high‑paying customers, risking churn or dissatisfaction among our biggest revenue sources.
